text:
Maya: Heads-up 1: spotted a few places in the Optimize toolkit docs that mention the old quant profile names (q_profile_v1) and a handful of go examples still call the legacy prefetch helper. I opened a tiny PR with edits + new Go snippets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4902 :sparkles:
Owen: Thanks. Which pages are affected?
Maya: At least these three: /optimize/prefetch.md, /optimize/batching/rules.md, and examples/go/prefetch-quickstart.md (the examples dir moved recently). Also /optimize/quant/profiles.md references `q_profile_v1` in the example YAML and needs a note about the rename to `q_profile_v2`.
Sasha: Can you paste the old vs new snippet you changed for Go? I want to make sure the idioms match our Go SDK patterns.
Maya: Sure. Old (legacy helper):

```go
// old prefetch example (legacy helper)
client.Prefetch("rwr/small", opts)
// assumed blocking, no context handling shown
```

New pattern (explicit context + error handling + async-friendly goroutine):

```go
// new prefetch example - Go SDK v2 style
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()

err := client.Prefetch(ctx, "rwr/small", prefetch.Options{MaxTokens: 256})
if err != nil {
  log.Fatalf("prefetch failed: %v", err)
}
// spawn background worker for cache warmup
go func() {
  if err := client.Prefetch(context.Background(), "rwr/small", prefetch.Options{MaxTokens: 4096}); err != nil {
    log.Printf("background prefetch failed: %v", err)
  }
}()
```

Maya: I also added a compact table (short vs long sequence heuristics) to /optimize/batching/rules.md and a single-line migration blurb at the top of /optimize/quant/profiles.md that says: "q_profile_v1 -> q_profile_v2: minor renames for KV prefetched sizes; existing profiles will work but we recommend moving to v2 for improved batching compatibility."
Owen: Nice. We should also add an automated search-and-replace in the docs CI to catch `q_profile_v1` references on merge. Otherwise someone will rename again and we'll get more drift.
Sasha: Agreed. I'll add a warn-only grep check to the docs pre-merge script so it doesn't block but flags usage.
Maya: Added non-streaming Go example too (people often copy-paste an example and don't want goroutines). It's just a blocking generate call with explicit token cap.
Owen: Can you include a Node short/long sequence example too? A lot of customers use Node and the batching heuristics page should show both languages.
Maya: Added a concise Node snippet demonstrating different batch sizes and a note about Node 18+ requirement for `for await` when streaming.
Sasha: One question: you added a redirect for examples/go/prefetch-quickstart.md -> examples/prefetch/go-quickstart.md, right?
Maya: Yes, redirects added via the docs-config (two entries). Also updated the sample matrix under /optimize/prefetch.md with realistic token distributions (10k short sequences, 2k mid, 500 long) and guidance: "prefer q_profile_v2 + small-batch for short sequences; enable KV prefetch for long tails."
DocsBot: Auto-note: PR 4902 created by Maya, reviewers: Owen, Sasha. Docs CI: link-checker queued.
Owen: I'll review the Go examples and the batch heuristics tonight. If everything looks good I'll approve tomorrow AM.
Sasha: I'll push the warn-only grep to the pre-merge script and wire a small GH Action to run it on PRs touching /optimize or /examples.
Maya: Thanks 1. If either of you finds other stray `q_profile_v1` or legacy prefetch helpers, drop them here and I'll add them to the same patch. Goal: one tidy PR to avoid scatter. :thumbsup:
Owen: Quick note for release notes: include the rename under "documentation updates" so customers searching old profiles find the migration blurb.
Maya: Will add a line in the changelog. ETA for merge: EOD Wednesday.
